newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria Sept state industrial output falls 12 pct.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria Sept state industrial output falls 12 pct.

text.p: Bulgarian state industrial output fell by 12 percent in September against the same month last year, the National Statistics Institute (NSI) said.

State industrial production totalled 148 billion levs in September, the lowest monthly level for the year so far calculated in January prices, and amounted to 827 billion levs for the first nine months, NSI figures showed.

However, the private sector, which accounts for some 14-17 percent of total industrial output, posted a real 6.0-percent year-on-year rise in September and a real 17-percent rise for the first nine months.

The rise was posted despite high interest rates and the declining number of orders in industry. The central interest rate rose from 34 percent annually in January to an all-time high of 300 percent in September.

Output in the state sector fell most in the chemical industry and oil processing and food and beverage industry with declines four times larger than the modest rise in production in the clothing industry, the NSI said.
Industrial output on both the state and private industrial sectors totalled 171 billion levs in current prices in September, down a real 10 percent against the same month of 1995, figures showed.
For the first nine months of this year, total industrial production in both sectors amounted to 959 billion levs in current prices, down a real one percent against the same period of last year.
